it'll clear up when it's ready to drink (2-3 months.) But, the longer the better with mead. so, at 2 months it may be clear, but the flavor will only get better with time.

Is that due to the slow fermentation, or sediment settling out? I started my first batch about a month back and have already noticed how much slower the process is than wine, even with yeast nutrients to supplement the nitrogen-poverty of honey.

mead and wine are similar in flavor development, imo. depends on what you put into it. citrus will also slow fermentation. acidity has an effect.

i've done the ancient orange small batch, and a couple batches of honey mead, as well as a few wine brews.

the wine batches have been a mixture of 4-week kits and longer-term fermentations. the longer-term kits do develop a great character on their own. the 4-week kits have (usually) horribly short shelf life, so i shy away from them now.

for me, for mead, the more time resting, no matter what the recipe, the better the character and flavor.

if you've got a batch of mead fermenting for a month, give it a try now, but another month will bring out more flavor and character. i'm not a big fan of mead, b/c i like beer, but i can fully appreciate the sweet heat that mead can bring.
